## Intent
Hypothesis: per-particle loop unrolling with component-wise NEON vectorization can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/particle FALLS from 11.382 at N=4000 to 7.795 at N=65000 — the L2 spill point (N≈61680) — then stays FLAT through N=4000000 (7.31 ns/p). The L1d spill at N≈963 lies below the smallest measured point. The cost drop across the L2→DRAM transition reflects overhead amortization, not a cache penalty: at N=4000 the 272 KB working set already exceeds L1d, so the curve spans only L2-resident to DRAM-resident with no spill knee. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: ~7.3 ns/p at q=0.01, ~9.0 at q=0.1, ~13.4 at q=0.5, flat across N in every series.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 9.3 GB/s at N=4000000, q=0.01 — 37% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.5 it falls to 5.04 GB/s (20%). The algo is never bandwidth-bound: at q=0.01 large N, compute is 70.5% and backend_stall 25.1%, placing it compute-bound. As death rate rises, branch_flush dominates — 37.2% at q=0.5 — transitioning to branch-bound. The transition is death-rate-driven, not N-driven; bandwidth is flat across N within each series.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. The update uses `ldr q1` (16-byte load), `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` (4-lane float), and `ext.16b` for lane rearrangement. An indexed load appears: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads one float into lane 1 from offset 0x14 within the 68-byte particle stride, assembling a vector from non-contiguous components. The loop is unrolled 4× (`ands x8, x25, #0xfffffffffffffffc`, increment by 4, stride 0x110=272=4×68). The render section's 31 `strb` byte stores with `ldrb`/`csel` saturation explain the 37% ceiling cap — scattered byte writes cannot stream. Five `udiv`/`msub` pairs implement spawn-index division in the respawn path.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo peaks at 9.3 GB/s (37% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01 and never approaches streaming bandwidth in any regime. Component-wise vectorization keeps it compute-bound (70.5%) rather than bandwidth-bound at low churn, but the byte-granular render scatter (31 `strb`) and branchy respawn (branch_flush 37.2% at q=0.5) prevent ceiling approach. The hypothesis fails even at q=0.01.
